1.text: James, a servant of God N of tha Lord Jesus Christ, 2 tha twelve tribes which r scattered abroad, greeting.
My brothers, count it all joy when y’all fall in2 divers temptations;
Knowin dis, dat tha trying of ur faith works patience.
But let patience have her perfect work, dat y’all may be perfect N entire, wantin nothing.
If any of u lack wisdom, let him ask of God, dat gives 2 all men liberally, N upbraideth not; N it will be given him.
But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. 4 he dat wavereth is like a wave of tha sea driven wit tha wind N tossed.
4 don’t let dat man think dat he shall receive any thing of tha Lord.
A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.
Let tha brother of low degree rejoice in dat he is exalted:
But tha rich, in dat he is made low: because as tha flower of tha grass he shall pass away.
4 tha sun is no sooner risen wit a burnin heat, but it withers tha grass, N tha flower of it falls, N tha grace of tha fashion of it perishes: so also shall tha rich man fade away in his ways.
Blessed is tha man dat endures temptation: 4 when he is tried, he shall receive tha crown of life, which tha Lord has promised 2 ’em dat love him.
Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: 4 God cannot be tempted wit evil, neither tempteth he any man:
But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, N enticed.
Then when lust has conceived, it brings forth sin: N sin, when it is finished, brings forth death.
Do not err, my beloved brothers.
Every good gift N every perfect gift is from above, N comes down from tha Father of lights, wit whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turnin.
Of his own will fathered he us wit tha word of truth, dat we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
So, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift 2 hear, slow 2 speak, slow 2 wrath:
4 tha wrath of man works not tha righteousness of God.
So lay apart all filthiness N superfluity of naughtiness, N receive wit meekness tha engrafted word, which is able 2 save ur souls.
But be y’all doers of tha word, N not hearers only, deceiving ur own selves.
4 if any be a hearer of tha word, N not a doer, he is like 2 a man beholding his natural face in a glass:
4 he beholdeth himself, N goes his way, N right away forgetteth what manner of man he was.
But whoever looks in2 tha perfect law of liberty, N continueth in it, he bein not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of tha work, dis man shall be blessed in his deed.
If any man among u seem 2 be religious, N bridleth not his tongue, but deceives his own heart, dis man’s religion is vain.
Pure religion N undefiled before God N tha Father is dis, 2 visit tha fatherless N widows in their affliction, N 2 keep himself unspotted from tha world.

2.text: My brothers, have not tha faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, tha Lord of glory, wit respect of persons.
4 if there come 2 ur assembly a man wit a gold ring, in goodly clothing, N there come in also a poor man in vile clothing;
N y’all have respect 2 him dat weareth tha gay clothing, N say 2 him, Sit u here in a good place; N say 2 tha poor, Stand u there, or sit here under my footstool:
R y’all not then partial in y’all, N r become judges of evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers, has not God chosen tha poor of dis world rich in faith, N heirs of tha kingdom which he has promised 2 ’em dat love him?
But y’all have despised tha poor. Do not rich men oppress u, N draw u before tha judgment seats?
Do not dey blaspheme dat worthy name by tha which y’all r called?
If y’all fulfil tha royal law according 2 tha scripture, u will love ur neighbour as urself, y’all do well:
But if y’all have respect 2 persons, y’all commit sin, N r convinced of tha law as transgressors.
4 whoever shall keep tha whole law, N yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
4 he dat said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if u commit no adultery, yet if u kill, u r become a transgressor of tha law.
So speak y’all, N so do, as dey dat shall be judged by tha law of liberty.
4 he shall have judgment without mercy, dat has showed no mercy; N mercy rejoices against judgment.
What does it profit, my brothers, though a man say he has faith, N have not works? can faith save him?
If a brother or sister be naked, N destitute of daily food,
N one of u say 2 ’em, Depart in peace, be y’all warmed N filled; even so y’all give ’em not dose things which r needful 2 tha body; what does it profit?
Even so faith, if it has not works, is dead, bein alone.
Yeah, a man may say, u have faith, N I have works: show me ur faith without ur works, N I will show u my faith by my works.
u believe dat there is one God; u do well: tha devils also believe, N tremble.
But will u know, O vain man, dat faith without works is dead?
Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon tha altar?
See u how faith wrought wit his works, N by works was faith made perfect?
N tha scripture was fulfilled which says, Abraham believed God, N it was imputed 2 him 4 righteousness: N he was called tha Friend of God.
y’all see then how dat by works a man is justified, N not by faith only.
Likewise also was not Rahab tha harlot justified by works, when she had received tha messengers, N had sent ’em out another way?
4 as tha body without tha spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

3.text: My brothers, don’t be many masters, knowin dat we shall receive tha greater condemnation.
4 in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, tha same is a perfect man, N able also 2 bridle tha whole body.
Look, we put bits in tha horses’ mouths, dat dey may obey us; N we turn about their whole body.
Look also tha ships, which though dey be so great, N r driven of fierce winds, yet r dey turned about wit a very small helm, wherever tha governor listeth.
Even so tha tongue is a little member, N boasteth great things. look, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!
N tha tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is tha tongue among our members, dat it defiles tha whole body, N sets on fire tha course of nature; N it is set on fire of hell.
4 every kind of beasts, N of birds, N of serpents, N of things in tha sea, is tamed, N has been tamed of mankind:
But tha tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
Wit it bless we God, even tha Father; N wit it curse we men, which r made after tha similitude of God.
Out of tha same mouth proceeds blessing N cursing. My brothers, dese things ought not so 2 be.
Does a fountain send forth at tha same place sweet water N bitter?
Can tha fig tree, my brothers, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so can no fountain both yield salt water N fresh.
Who is a wise man N endued wit knowledge among u? let him show out of a good conversation his works wit meekness of wisdom.
But if y’all have bitter envying N strife in ur hearts, glory not, N lie not against tha truth.
Dis wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.
4 where envying N strife is, there is confusion N every evil work.
But tha wisdom dat is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, N easy 2 be intreated, full of mercy N good fruits, without partiality, N without hypocrisy.
N tha fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of ’em dat make peace.

4.text: From from where come wars N fightings among u? come dey not hence, even of ur lusts dat war in ur members?
y’all lust, N have not: y’all kill, N desire 2 have, N cannot obtain: y’all fight N war, yet y’all have not, because y’all ask not.
y’all ask, N receive not, because y’all ask amiss, dat y’all may consume it upon ur lusts.
y’all adulterers N adulteresses, know y’all not dat tha friendship of tha world is enmity wit God? whoever therefore will be a friend of tha world is tha opp of God.
Do y’all think dat tha scripture says in vain, tha spirit dat lives in us lusteth 2 envy?
But he gives more grace. so he says, God resisteth tha proud, but gives grace 2 tha humble.
Submit y’all therefore 2 God. Resist tha devil, N he will flee from u.
Draw nigh 2 God, N he will draw nigh 2 u. Cleanse ur hands, y’all sinners; N purify ur hearts, y’all double minded.
Be afflicted, N mourn, N weep: let ur laughter be turned 2 mournin, N ur joy 2 heaviness.
Humble y’all in tha sight of tha Lord, N he shall lift u up.

Speak not evil one of another, brothers. He dat speaks evil of his brother, N judges his brother, speaks evil of tha law, N judges tha law: but if u judge tha law, u r not a doer of tha law, but a judge.
There is one lawgiver, who is able 2 save N 2 destroy: who r u dat judge another?
Go 2 now, y’all dat say, 2 day or 2 morrow we will go in2 such a city, N continue there a year, N buy N sell, N get gain:
Whereas y’all know not what shall be on tha morrow. 4 what is ur life? It is even a vapour, dat appears 4 a little time, N then vanisheth away.
4 dat y’all ought 2 say, If tha Lord will, we shall live, N do dis, or dat.
But now y’all rejoice in ur boastings: all such rejoicin is evil.
Therefore 2 him dat knows 2 do good, N does it not, 2 him it is sin.

5.text: Go 2 now, y’all rich men, weep N howl 4 ur miseries dat shall come upon u.
Ur riches r corrupted, N ur garments r motheaten.
Ur gold N silver is cankered; N tha rust of ’em shall be a witness against u, N shall eat ur flesh as it were fire. y’all have heaped treasure together 4 tha last days.
Look, tha hire of tha labourers who have reaped down ur fields, which is of u kept back by fraud, cries: N tha cries of ’em which have reaped r entered in2 tha ears of tha Lord of sabaoth.
y’all have lived in pleasure on tha earth, N been wanton; y’all have nourished ur hearts, as in a day of slaughter.
y’all have condemned N killed tha just; N he does not resist u.
Be patient therefore, brothers, 2 tha comin of tha Lord. look, tha husbandman waits 4 tha precious fruit of tha earth, N has long patience 4 it, until he receive tha early N latter rain.
Be y’all also patient; stablish ur hearts: 4 tha comin of tha Lord draws nigh.
Grudge not one against another, brothers, lest y’all be condemned: look, tha judge stands before tha door.
Take, my brothers, tha prophets, who have spoken in tha name of tha Lord, 4 an example of sufferin affliction, N of patience.
Look, we count ’em happy which endure. y’all have heard of tha patience of Job, N have seen tha end of tha Lord; dat tha Lord is very pitiful, N of tender mercy.
But above all things, my brothers, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by tha earth, neither by any other oath: but let ur yeah be yeah; N ur no, no; lest y’all fall in2 condemnation.
Is any among u afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.
Is any sick among u? let him call 4 tha elders of tha church; N let ’em pray over him, anointing him wit oil in tha name of tha Lord:
N tha prayer of faith shall save tha sick, N tha Lord shall raise him up; N if he have committed sins, dey shall be forgiven him.
Confess ur faults one 2 another, N pray one 4 another, dat y’all may be healed. tha effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
Elias was a man subject 2 like passions as we r, N he prayed earnestly dat it might not rain: N it rained not on tha earth by tha space of three years N six months.
N he prayed again, N tha heaven gave rain, N tha earth brought forth her fruit.
Brothers, if any of u do err from tha truth, N one convert him;
Let him know, dat he which converteth tha sinner from tha error of his way shall save a soul from death, N shall hide a crowd of sins.
